jobs.description:
The Department of Biomedicine at Faculty of Health at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as Postdoc in the field of translational neuropsychiatry as per 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a fixed-term full-time position for 2 years with the possibility of extension.

The Department of Biomedicine prioritises diversity and a good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for groundbreaking research. In a diverse and international research environment, dedicated employees are looking to generate new knowledge within biomedical research areas such as infection and inflammation, membranes, neuroscience and personalised medicine. The Department of Biomedicine provides research-based teaching of the highest quality and is responsible for a large part of the medical degree programme. Academic staff contribute to the teaching. English is the preferred language in the laboratory, at meetings and at seminars. The department employs approx. 500 people from all over the world, and they make use of the department's modern laboratory-, core- and animal facilities. The Department of Biomedicine focuses on innovation, entrepreneurship and collaboration with business and industry, and numerous researchers from the department have established companies to develop new medicinal treatments founded in professional scientific basic research. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

About the research project
The project will investigate the mechanisms by which emotional imbalance regulates transcriptional programs and structural connectivity in disease-relevant brain regions in rodents. A drug candidate will be evaluated using these experimental paradigms and behavioral phenotyping.

Your job responsibilities
As Postdoc in translational psychiatry your position is primarily research-based but may also involve teaching assignments. You will contribute to the development of the department through research of high international quality. In your daily work, you will work closely with colleagues on your project, where you will receive supervision and guidance.

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Independent research of high international quality, including publication.
• Conduct spatial and cell-specific molecular profiling using approaches such as RNAscope multiplex, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
• Investigate, design, conduct, and analyze behavioral experiments in rodent models of depression, stress susceptibility, and resilience.
• Characterization of neuronal network structure by whole brain imaging
• You will work closely with the project leaders and collaborators in molecular neuroscience, neuropharmacology, and preclinical imaging.
You will report to Professor Anders Nykjaer, Director of PROMEMO, Dept. of Biomedicine.

Your competences 
You have a PhD in neuroscience and experience in experimental neuropharmacology or a closely related field. The candidate must have completed his/her graduate education abroad. Solid experience with confocal and light-sheet microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, and the analysis of complex molecular or cellular datasets is required. The successful candidate is also expected to have experience conducting behavioural experiments using rodent models of depression, stress susceptibility, or resilience.

As a person, you have good interpersonal skills, are inclusive and team-oriented and able to contribute to a good work environment. We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English.

In order to be assessed as qualified for a Postdoc position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

To be considered for the position, applicants must meet the formal requirements for academic appointments at Aarhus University and submit all required application materials by the deadline. Applications that are substantially incomplete will not proceed to further assessment.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Anders Nykjaer, email: an@biomed.au.dk.

Your place of work will be the Department of Biomedicine, Høegh-Guldbergs Gade 10, bldg. 1116, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

We expect to conduct interviews in week 44-45.

Terms of employment 
• Appointment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.
• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• The yearly base salary for a fulltime postdoc is between DKK 493.394,35 and DKK 585.322,48 depending on the years of working experience after achieved MSc degree. The base salary includes a position related supplement and pension (18.07 %). Additional supplement(s) for special qualifications can be negotiated. Authorisation supplemement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.
• Researchers recruited from abroad are offered a special researcher tax scheme with a lower tax rate.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff

Application
Your application must include the following:

• Motivated application
• Curriculum Vitae
• Diploma
• Template for applicant - postdoc
• A list of publications
• A teaching portfolio. We refer to Guideline on the use of teaching portfolios
• A maximum of five of the publications of greatest relevance to the job may be submitted (optional)
• Research plan can be uploaded (optional)
• Coauthor statement(s) can be uploaded (optional)
• References/recommendations can be uploaded separately in the e-recruitment system (optional)
We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

International applicant?
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including assistance with relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about the International Staff Office and the range of services here. Aarhus University also has a Junior Researcher Association and offers career development support. You can read more about these resources here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in fermentation-based production of biochemicals - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about sustainability and reducing environmental impact through biomanufacturing? Then come join us in developing advancing technologies for fermenting robust microbial cell factories and scalable bioprocesses that convert CO₂-derived feedstocks into high-volume chemicals. This multi-year initiative consists of joint efforts between multiple groups covering the entire innovation pipeline, from metabolic tools and design, strain engineering, process design, fermentation, downstream processing, multi-omics, techno-economic validation, and business development. We aim to establish new industrial routes for essential chemicals in a low-carbon economy through interdisciplinary collaboration.

Are you establishing your career as scientist and are you looking for the best possible foundation for carrying out research on production of biochemicals from CO2-derived substrates?

You will play a key role in a project coordinated by Professor Alex Toftgaard Nielsen at BRIGHT (Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition) at the Technical University of Denmark

You will be involved in developing fermentation and downstream processes for production of biochemicals from mixed C1-derived substrates. The goal is to develop microbial production systems that radically change the production of chemicals in our society.

Responsibilities and qualifications

Your primary focus will be to:

• Optimizing fermentation conditions for selected processes under both anaerobic and aerobic processes. 
• Carry out media optimization experiments to identify limiting substrates. 
• Be involved in carrying out and analyzing proteomics and transcriptomics experiments.
• Contribute to developing downstream processes for purification of selected products.
• Help establish titer, rate and yield requirements for economically relevant processes.
• Collaborate with an interdisciplinary team of researchers.
• Contribute to publishing research findings in high-impact scientific journals. 
• Prepare technical reports, presentations, as well as project deliverables ensuring high levels of accuracy and presentation.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

We are looking for a candidate with a background in fermentation and downstream processes, ideally combined with:

• Hands-on experience with cultivation of anaerobic bacteria, including Clostridium sp., as well as aerobic organisms, including for example S. cerevisiae.
• Hands-on experience with anaerobic cultivation methods.
• Experience with process modelling and basic programming skills is an advantage.
• Excellent communication skills and an openness to interdisciplinary teamwork.
Solid English capabilities are required, and you will be involved in teaching and supervision of BSc and MSc student projects.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Alex Toftgaard Nielsen. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Start date is 01-01-2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Alex Toftgaard Nielsen. 

You can read more at www.bright.dtu.dk 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 3 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRiGHT) at DTU.
Recent progress in our ability to read and write genomic code, combined with advances in automation, analytics and data science, has fundamentally changed the scope and ambition of harnessing the potential of biological systems. Big data approaches and analysis of biological systems are key research instruments at the Institute. BRiGHT utilizes these advances for mission driven microbial cell factory design to foster sustainable lifestyles in relation to three application areas: Sustainable materials, Microbial Foods, and Net-zero agriculture.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor (tenure track)/Associate Professor in Computational end Generative Design
jobs.description:
Are you interested in scientific computing, artificial intelligence, and how they can automate and enhance design of civil engineering structures? Are you interested in creating societal impact with your research? Then the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering of Aarhus University invites you to apply for this position.

Expected start date and duration of employment
The expected starting date is no later than August 1 2027.

Job description
This position is part of the section for Structural Engineering.
Your tasks will be:

• Teaching/upgrading existing courses related to Structural Engineering at both B.Sc. and M.Sc. level in Civil and Architectural Engineering programmes.
• Supervising students at different levels (e.g., multidisciplinary projects, master theses, doctoral theses).
• Conducting research through externally sponsored grants at national and international levels.
• Establishing relevant collaborations with the Danish industry.
• Contributing to the operation of the department.
Your profile
We are looking for a candidate that can enhance the department’s competencies in computational design. The candidate shall hold:

• Engineering background (B.Sc. and M.Sc.).
• Doctoral degree in a relevant field of research.
• High-level proficiency in English.
The following qualifications and experience are required:

• Scientific computing, possibly with different programming languages (e.g., Python, Julia, C#, C++ MATLAB).
• Parametric and algorithmic building design using, e.g., Rhino/Grasshopper tool suite.
• Physics-informed machine learning, generative and agentic AI for building design automation.
• Teaching and developing computational and generative design courses related to structural engineering.
• Supervision of undergraduate and graduate students (B.Sc., M.Sc., and Ph.D. theses).
Candidates must demonstrate potential for outstanding research and teaching. The selected candidate shall demonstrate:

• Some years of post-graduate research and publication experience are required. A pre-existing and growing international research network is expected. Prior collaboration with the Danish innovation ecosystem is desired, but not essential.
• Experience from successful external research collaborations with industry and academia, project management skills. Experience in the attraction of external funding is preferred.
• Research ability documented through rising publication and citation records evidenced by appropriate bibliometric parameters in reputable international peerreviewed journals.
Well-defined research focus and sound strategy to develop a research group.

Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students. We conduct research and education within structural engineering, geotechnics, architectural engineering and design, sustainability, construction management, climate adaptation, indoor climate, building materials, and digital technologies.

The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public-sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners. The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities. We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators. Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue. The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance. The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Navitas, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. The area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Giuseppe Abbiati +45 93 52 17 51, abbiati@cae.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than December 14 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Process specialist in Nanofabrication to the Niels Bohr Institute
jobs.employer_name: KU- SCIENCE - CHEM og MATH og NBI-HCØ
jobs.description:
The NBI Cleanroom facility at the Niels Bohr Institute seeks an innovative candidate for a time-limited, part-time (8 hours per week) technical position as Process specialist in Nanofabrication.

The NBI Cleanroom is a research infrastructure providing nanofabrication, processing and characterization facilities to the research groups of NBI. With a focus on quantum electronics and quantum photonics, the research and innovation is mainly driven by The Center for Quantum Devices (Q-Dev) www.qdev.dk, Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks (Hy-Q) www.hy-q.nbi.ku.dk, and The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) https://nqcp.ku.dk, involving coordinated activity in materials growth, processing, characterization, and nanoscale fabrication. The cleanroom also accommodates external commercial user groups.

The position
The candidate will join the department’s existing team of lab technicians and engineers. The tasks within the position are among others to develop processes in close collaboration with researchers and students allowing the fabrication of novel nanostructures for basic and applied research in electronics and other nanodevice applications. This will require the integration of multiple tools and methods, as well as the development of new nanofabrication methods. 

The candidate is expected to contribute within the following areas:

• 
Supervise and train researchers, postdocs and students and other technical staff in using research equipment.

• 
Developing state of the art processes within areas such as Electron Beam Lithography, UV-Lithography, Physical Vapor Deposition, Molecular Beam Epitaxy and Atomic Layer Deposition.

• 
Manage technical collaborations with research teams for the development of the nanofabrication facility.

• 
Maintain and trouble-shoot research equipment in collaboration with technical staff and run regular calibration procedures on the tools.

• 
Share responsibilities for tools and processes and purchases with other members of the technical staff.

Profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic candidate with the following competencies and experience:

• 
Candidates should have a MSc or PhD degree in Electrical engineering or Physics or an equivalent relevant degree.

• 
An in-depth understanding of laboratory safety, and experience with hazardous tools and materials associated with nanofabrication facilities is required.

• 
Thorough knowledge about nanofabrication procedures with emphasis on electron beam lithography preferably using Elionix and Raith tools and skills necessary to design the entire fabrication process.

• 
Experience with device and materials characterization/imaging tools such as scanning probe and scanning/transmission electron microscopy.

• 
Have knowledge about a broad spectrum of nanofabrication methods, semiconductor physics, electronics, physics, mechanical and electrical engineering.

• 
Have cleanroom experience.

Terms of salary and employment
The position is part-time (8 hours per week) and is fixed for a 2-year term. The position is scheduled to start 1 December 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter.
Employment will be as academic employee or special consultant, and the salary is based on seniority. Employment will be under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Application
If you are interested in the position, please submit your electronic application, including attachments, via the UCPH Job Portal (click the “APPLY NOW” link at the bottom of the job posting).

• 
Letter of application addressing the requirements (max. one page).

• 
Current curriculum Vitae

• 
Letters of reference

• 
A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education

 Deadline for applications is 4 November 2026

The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. 

Further Information 
Questions regarding the position may be directed to Cleanroom Lab Manager Martin Saurbrey Bjergfelt, mail: martin.bjergfelt@nbi.ku.dk, phone +45 23 81 08 93.

Copenhagen or Skive - Fluent German speaking

Are you motivated by converting open opportunities into structured sales activity through disciplined follow-up and strong CRM habits? Do you thrive in a role where customer engagement, data insight and account development go hand in hand? If you bring experience from sales-oriented roles and a highly organised, self-driven way of working, you might be the new colleague we are looking for to strengthen our German sales organisation. Mastery of German and English, both spoken and written, is a must.

Take ownership of converting opportunities into revenue across Germany

Reporting to the Sales Manager for Germany, you will strengthen customer engagement, improve lead conversion and maximise revenue opportunities through structured follow-up, proactive communication and CRM discipline. You will act as a dedicated Internal Account Manager, converting open opportunities into measurable sales activities while supporting the Area Sales Managers with better insights, better data and more qualified customer interactions. Your primary tasks and responsibilities will be:

• Proactively identify leads for new business opportunities and work systematically in CRM according to the Vikan Sales Excellence Processes, including updating contact persons, creating tasks and scheduling appointments
• Build relationships with key end users and position Vikan as the preferred partner and supplier, identifying opportunities for solution selling and category expansion within key accounts
• Work with the German Sales team to secure more POS data, and analyse data and trends to create sales opportunities for the sales team
• Support Area Sales Managers with insights and tools for local engagement, utilise Salesforce dashboards, and book meetings on their behalf
• Increase the number and conversion of site surveys by engaging accounts
• Drive Shadow Board aftersales and reorder growth by re-engaging customers
• Convert direct deliveries into site surveys and additional revenue through follow-ups aligned with distributor agreements
• Strengthen relationships with key end users through quarterly follow-ups, ensuring continuity, satisfaction and early identification of emerging needs
• Increase awareness and sales of new and strategically important products, including introducing key end users to new product ranges, promoting focus products and following up on sample products
Structured, self-driven profile with good commercial skills

You bring experience from internal sales, account management or business development, combined with strong business and sales concept orientation and solid commercial and negotiation skills. jobs.description:
Are you ready to lead impactful construction projects that shape the future of pharmaceutical manufacturing - while fostering a safe, collaborative, and inclusive work environment? Then we hope to hear from you.

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

As the Senior Manager of Construction Management, you will contribute to keep strengthening our competencies, deliver high-quality results and to the strategy for the Construction Management function. You will also collaborate across departments to ensure alignment with broader business objectives.

Your leadership style should be passionate about creating a culture where people thrive, and you understand that high performance is built on trust, engagement, and a shared purpose – building on the foundation of NNE leadership principles. This is a unique opportunity to lead our organisation into effective operations, high compliance standards and a strong business focus.

How you might spend your days

As Senior Manager of Construction Management, you’ll:

• Lead and develop a high-performing construction management, while developing team capabilities and well-being

• Ensure successful project execution through effective site mobilisation and risk management

• Establish and continuously improve systems for construction management, including planning, resourcing, and budgeting.

• Build and manage effective client relationships on site, ensuring stakeholder alignment and project success.

• Ensure compliance with project plans, NNE’s quality standards, and execution model.

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Translate high-level goals into actionable plans and guide your team through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.

• Ability to mentor and coach team members across experience levels.

• Understand industry challenges, make informed decisions and take ownership of results.

• Embrace innovation and continuous learning, especially in digital tools.

• Contribute with a thoughtful and purpose-driven work style, and model the values and standards expected across the organization.

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• Degree in engineering or a related technical field (M.Sc. or B.Sc.)

• Experience in construction and site management (typically 8-10 years)

• Experience establishing and developing systems within this field (including construction and commissioning planning, systems for managing temporary work and installations, etc.)

• Familiarity with 4D/5D tools and digital construction management.

• Commitment to safety and experience in safety-critical environments.

• Proficiency in English.

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 31st October 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Director of Project Management Jens Roy Krejberg Simonsen at +45 30796136.

Please note:

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

******Join Our Team at Devote Consulting

****Are you an experienced AI/ML professional with a passion for applying emerging technologies to solve complex business challenges within Life Sciences? Do you enjoy working closely with clients, building relationships, and turning innovative ideas into practical solutions?

Devote Consulting is expanding its team and is looking for Senior Consultants with expertise in AI/ML and generative AI (genAI) implementation in regulated life sciences environments.

****Are We Looking for You?

• You thrive in the dynamic world of consulting and enjoy leading innovation in emerging technologies

• You combine strong technical AI/ML expertise with excellent communication and stakeholder management skills

• You take ownership of your work, driving high-quality outcomes that create business value while ensuring compliance

• You have experience delivering AI-driven solutions and improving processes within Life Sciences

• You enjoy translating complex technologies into practical solutions and helping clients navigate change

****As a Senior Consultant at Devote Consulting, your key responsibilities will include:

• AI/ML implementation: Lead and support the implementation of generative AI use cases in life sciences and drive AI-driven transformation in R&D, clinical operations, and regulatory affairs

• Business process optimization: (Re)design and enhance workflows by integrating AI-driven solutions, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and scalability in regulated environments

**Your Qualifications

• A master’s degree in Computer Science, IT, Engineering, Data Science, Life Sciences, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience in AI/ML development, implementation, or platform engineering, including hands-on experience with generative AI or large language models (LLMs)

• Professional experience within Life Sciences (Pharma, Biotech, or MedTech), with an understanding of regulatory requirements

• Experience with software validation, GxP compliance, or related documentation in regulated environments

• Strong consulting and stakeholder management skills, with experience in client-facing roles and the ability to translate complex technical solutions into business value

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with fluency in English and a genuine interest in working closely with clients

****What We Offer

****At Devote Consulting, you'll have the opportunity to take responsibility, lead initiatives, and help shape the future of AI within Life Sciences.

You'll work directly with clients on projects where you can combine your technical expertise with consulting, business process improvement, and stakeholder management. Depending on the project, you may take on responsibilities as a specialist, business analyst, or project manager.

You'll become part of a collaborative, high-achieving consulting environment where professional development, knowledge sharing, and personal growth are highly valued.

****Ready to Join Us?

****We welcome individuals from all backgrounds and are committed to a recruitment process that ensures equal opportunities for all applicants. We review applications on a rolling basis, so apply today!

Forward Deployed AI Engineer

Engineering, Full time, Remote (EU), Berlin, Copenhagen, or Milan

**About Apylon And The Opportunity

**Apylon is building agents for the most complex workflow out there - financial admin in healthcare.

Hospitals and payers move billions of euros through fragmented, manual workflows shaped by clinical data, payer rules, contracts, and local coding systems. We believe this is a data, machine-learning, and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

We are live with leading private hospitals and expanding quickly. Every hospital presents a different challenge: EHR systems are configured differently, national coding rules vary, and contracts describe the same clinical event in different terms. Your job is to help us turn that complexity into a system that learns: each new integration should make the next one faster, safer, and less expensive.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe. You’ll join the first small engineering team, with massive ownership over both what we build and how we build it.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Own EHR integrations end to end: APIs, schemas, undocumented behaviour, operational failure modes, and vendor changes.

• Build reusable integration-platform primitives for extraction, normalisation, versioning, replay, monitoring, and observability.

• Design the canonical data model that connects heterogeneous EHR data, reimbursement systems, national coding standards, and hospital-specific conventions.

• Build reliable inputs for our billing agents, including the constraints, validation, and evaluation systems that make model-assisted decisions safe to use in production.

• Work directly with hospital IT teams and EHR vendors: technical discovery, implementation, joint debugging, and onboarding.

• Take responsibility for the full lifecycle of your work: design, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iteration from real-world data.

Who you are

• 3+ years building and operating production systems in complex, messy domains. We care more about demonstrated judgment and ownership than an exact number of years.

• Experience using LLMs as production components—not just developer tools. You understand when to use models, when deterministic systems are better, how to constrain outputs, and how to evaluate reliability.

• Strong data-modelling instincts. You know when abstraction creates leverage and when it hides important real-world variation.

• Comfort working from incomplete information. You form hypotheses, test them against data, and distinguish unknowns that can wait from assumptions that could invalidate the system.

• Confidence in customer-facing technical work: discovery calls, debugging sessions, and direct conversations with vendors and hospital IT teams.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

• A practical, hands-on approach: equally comfortable designing an integration architecture and writing a quick script to answer an urgent question.

This role may be a strong fit if

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

What this role is not

• Consulting or bespoke delivery work. Each integration must improve the product and reduce the marginal cost of the next.

• A role insulated from customers or operational reality.

• Pure platform engineering or pure integration work: the value comes from doing both.

• A role where incorrect mappings are merely technical defects. In this domain, they can produce incorrect invoices.

Bonus points

• Experience with healthcare interoperability or coding standards, including HL7v2, FHIR, or national messaging and reimbursement standards.

• Experience building and operating third-party integrations at scale.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.

• Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company.

• Working proficiency in Danish, or German.

Our tech stack

• Python

• Django

• React

• PostgreSQL

• AWS

• K8s

• Terraform

• Bedrock

• We’re pragmatic. You’ll have a big say in how it evolves.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us during workdays at the office.

• Regular off-sites and social events. We like building together, not just working together.

• Travel within the EU roughly monthly. Onboarding a hospital, working through an integration with a vendor’s engineers, or spending time on-site to understand how the data is actually produced. If travelling to a hospital basement to figure out why an export is malformed sounds like a bad week, this isn’t your role.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code, powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue systems.

How to apply. If you're excited by the challenge of building intelligent, high-impact systems at the core of European healthcare and enjoy shipping fast, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on, resourceful Forward Deployed Engineer to join our Technical Operations team.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Templafy, you will play a critical role in supporting our growth by working directly with strategic customers to design, build, and deploy tailored solutions that bring Templafy’s platform into their real-world environments.

You will take deep technical ownership of the customer journey—from initial discovery and solution design through implementation and launch. You’ll work closely with customers to understand their most complex document workflows and build the environments, integrations, and AI-powered solutions needed to solve them.

This is a highly collaborative and customer-facing role that sits at the intersection of engineering, product, and commercial strategy.

What You’ll Do

Embedded Customer Engineering

Work on-site or virtually alongside strategic customers to build, configure, and integrate Templafy solutions directly into their document workflows.

Custom Solution Development

Design and build tailored customer environments using their content, business rules, integrations, knowledge, and data to address complex document use cases and deliver solutions that meet their specific needs.

Technical Discovery & Architecture Mapping

Rapid Prototyping

Product Collaboration

Deployment & Change Management

What We’re Looking For

• Ability to identify gaps during discovery and proactively engage the appropriate customer stakeholders to gather the information needed to move forward.

• Experience working with REST APIs, enterprise integrations, authentication/SSO, and automation frameworks.

• Strong technical curiosity and interest in AI. Experience integrating with or building on top of LLM providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic is a strong plus.

• Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments and turning loosely defined customer problems into working software.

• Ability to clearly communicate technical concepts, recommendations, and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Understanding of enterprise document governance and workflows, with the confidence to engage directly with senior and C-level IT stakeholders.

• Strong technical and user-facing knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word and PowerPoint, and their file structures is a plus.

How We’ll Measure Success

Success in this role will include:

Employee Benefits:

At Templafy, we’re all about building an inclusive culture where talented people come together to spark creativity in a dynamic, collaborative space. jobs.occupation: Experienced Consultant for Enterprise Cost Steering Team
jobs.description:
**Job Description

**_Are you ready to play a key role in transforming resource allocation at one of the leading financial institutions? Join our Enterprise Cost Steering team to lead initiatives that improve financial health through strategic cost optimization. This position offers a unique opportunity to influence cost efficiency strategies Group-wide.

_**What You Will Be Doing

**As an Experienced Consultant in Enterprise Cost Steering, you will support the executive leadership team with insights and recommendations to optimize cost structures. Working closely with Finance teams, Procurement, Support functions, and Business Units, you will identify cost-optimizing opportunities and implement best practices that strengthen our financial foundation.

• Own, drive, coordinate and execute end-to-end cost efficiency initiatives across the Group, including planning, tracking progress and managing delivery against agreed milestones

• Apply strong critical thinking by questioning assumptions and provide well-reasoned recommendations

• Leverage data analytics to conduct comprehensive cost analysis and identify cost efficiency opportunities

• Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to design and implement cost steering frameworks, ensuring clear governance, roles and responsibilities

• Translate complex data into actionable insights for senior leadership

• Act as trusted partner providing expert guidance on strategic cost initiatives

• Build and maintain dashboards and tools to support ongoing cost analysis, generating actionable insights, reporting and decision-making

• Facilitate workshops to align stakeholders and build consensus on initiatives and drive agreed actions to completion

**About You

**

• Strong consulting and project management background, with experience delivering strategic solutions in complex organisations

• Solid experience in enterprise-level cost steering or strategic cost management

• Excellent problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail

• Proven ability to independently manage initiatives from ideation through execution, including defining scope, plans, milestones, dependencies and delivery risks

• Strong critical thinking skills with ability to challenge assumptions

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management, with the ability to engage, influence and build trust across all levels while maintaining alignment, accountability and momentum

• Advanced skills in data analysis, reporting and visualisation tools

• Master's degree in finance, economics, business administration or similar

You thrive in dynamic environments with evolving priorities and demonstrate collaborative teamwork alongside quantitative expertise to support strategic decision-making.

**What We Offer You

**You will join a supportive team that values collaboration and professional growth. We offer hybrid working with 3 to 4 days per week in the office to promote knowledge sharing and culture building. You will have opportunities to develop your expertise while making meaningful contributions to our financial health and cost efficiency initiatives.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**We would love to hear from you if this opportunity excites you. Please reach out to Hadis Atighi at kho@danskebank.dk for any questions about the role. We process applications continuously, so we encourage you to apply sooner rather than later.

We look forward to receiving your application!

All Gravy is the AI-native people operating platform for hospitality and retail. 🥞

We're modernising how frontline teams work, replacing scattered tools and outdated systems with a single app that's actually built for the way people work & socialise today. Our AI Colleague gives staff instant answers & executes day-to-day tasks, freeing up managers to focus on people & customers instead of paperwork. We work with some of the most exciting brands in hospitality and retail, including Gail's, L'Osteria, Dishoom, Pizza Pilgrims, Ottolenghi, Q8 and 7-Eleven. Today over 2,000 restaurants and stores trust us to run their teams.

We've grown 10x in two years and are accelerating into new markets. Our team spans a wide range of nationalities and backgrounds, united by one mission: to create better work lives for the 80% of the world that do not sit behind a desk. 🚀

🤩 **About the role

**We are looking for an AI Engineer to build the AI layer of All Gravy: agents that plan shifts, answer manager questions, and take real actions across 2,000+ hospitality and retail locations in the Nordics and UK.

This is a build role, not a research role. You will ship agents that customers use in production, then own how well they work. We are looking for someone who has already built and shipped AI agents and who is relentlessly curious about what just became possible. The field moves faster than any roadmap, so part of the job is noticing the new capability before anyone asks you to, testing it, and telling us whether it changes what we should build.

🎯 **What you will do

**

• Build agent harnesses. Design and ship agents that call internal and external tools to solve real customer problems, both interactively with users and autonomously in the background.

• Own the eval loop. Build the harnesses, datasets, and offline and online evals that tell us whether an agent got better or worse. You define what "working" means and you defend the number.

• Ship full stack. Take features end to end, from the manager and employee interfaces where schedules are built and shifts are picked up, through the backend services and data layers that power them.

• Run it in production. Own latency, cost, failure modes, and guardrails for the agents you ship. When one misbehaves at 6am on a Saturday, you are the person who understands why.

• Investigate what is new. Try the new models, frameworks, and techniques as they land, build small things to find out where they actually hold up, and bring back a clear read on what we should adopt and what we should ignore.

• Work across teams. Partner with product and the other engineering teams so AI features fit the wider All Gravy ecosystem, and contribute to shared standards and architectural decisions.

✅ **What we are looking for

**

• You have built agents that shipped to real users, not just demos. You can talk through what broke, what you changed, and what you would do differently.

• Genuine curiosity, evidenced by things you built. You have side projects, throwaway experiments, or strong opinions formed by actually running the thing rather than reading about it.

• Strong context and prompt engineering, including retrieval, tool design, and structured outputs. You know why an agent fails and it is usually not the model.

• Solid production engineering in TypeScript and Node.js, or the ability to get there fast from another typed language.

• Comfort reading and writing code, reviewing architecture, and working directly with infrastructure. You ship the fix rather than filing the ticket.

• Judgment about when an agent is the right answer and when a well placed SQL query or a boring deterministic rule is better.

🙌 **You'll thrive here if you

**We're looking for people with great energy, a good sense of humour, and a drive for getting things over the line. You think elegantly but act pragmatically, love being part of a team, and never stop learning

• 5+ years of proven full-stack experience across React, React Native, TypeScript, and Node.js.

• Ability to design and architect highly available, fault-tolerant, and scalable distributed systems.

• Startup or scale-up background. You know what it means to move fast, make pragmatic calls, and revisit them when the time is right.

• Fluent English, spoken and written.

• Based within European time zones, whether from our Copenhagen or London office or remotely.

An advantage if you have experience in:

• Vercel AI SDK

• Mastra or similar Agent framework

💎 **Why All Gravy

**

• Grow fast, for real. We promote from within, move quickly, and give you real responsibility from day one.

• Top equipment. You'll receive all new equipment to do your best work

• A culture that actually develops you. Honest feedback, active coaching, and the autonomy to experiment. We invest in you because your growth is our growth.

• Work that matters. Your work will directly impact the daily lives of millions of frontline workers.

• You'll work with people who've built, scaled, and won. Ex-founders, operators, all here because they want to do it again, bigger.

• The good stuff too. Prime office location, team lunches, Friday bars, padel tournaments, wine tastings, offsites, top-tier equipment, and a fridge that's always stocked. We work hard and celebrate harder.

💡 Even if you do not tick every box on this page, you might be the perfect fit for the job! We treasure our learning culture and encourage all humble people to apply.
